name: Libertarian Traditionalist
description: Free-market individualism blended with traditional values. Mostly self-consistent, but reveals real internal tensions between personal liberty and social conservatism.
beliefs: Free markets allocate resources more efficiently than central planning
Individual liberty is the highest political value
Traditional family structures are the backbone of a stable society
Government regulation usually does more harm than good
Personal responsibility matters more than systemic factors
A strong national defense is essential for freedom
Religious values provide the best moral foundation
Property rights are the cornerstone of all other rights
Immigration should be tightly controlled to preserve culture
People should be free to live however they choose

justifications.1-9: Individual liberty and the freedom to live however one chooses are nearly synonymous — both center personal autonomy as the highest value.
justifications.1-8: The belief in individual liberty as the highest value tensions with immigration control, which restricts others' liberty to move freely.
justifications.2-9: Traditional family structures as a social imperative conflicts with the principle that people should live however they choose.
justifications.6-9: Religious moral foundations imply behavioral norms that constrain the freedom to live however one chooses.
justifications.8-9: Tight immigration control to preserve culture directly contradicts the principle that people should be free to live as they choose.
justifications.0-3: Free market efficiency and opposition to government regulation are mutually reinforcing — both advocate minimal state interference in economics.
justifications.2-6: Traditional family values and religious moral foundations share the same conservative cultural worldview.
justifications.0-1: Free market advocacy and individual liberty are both grounded in the primacy of voluntary exchange and personal autonomy.
